GuideIntro: Open a topic below. This guide covers all five demo roles. The screenshots use sample records. The names and available buttons in your own account depend on your data and role.
GuideSignInText: After opening the application, enter your Fleet Management username and password. Select Sign in or press Enter. Use the selector in the upper-right corner to choose Русский or English. The language changes immediately. Select Registration if you need an account.
GuideSignInImage: The sign-in window. The language selector is on the upper right.
GuideRegistrationText: On the Registration screen, enter a username, a password and the same password again. Open Demo role and choose one option. Select Create account. When the account is ready, the application returns to sign-in with the username filled in. Enter the password and select Sign in. Back to sign-in closes registration and clears both password fields. Usernames must be unique. For example, “operator” and “Operator” count as the same username.
GuideRegistrationImage: The registration form. Choose a demo role after entering your username and password.
GuideRolesText:
Director manages the main tables, reference data and links. Vehicles requiring repair is a view-only list.
Passenger dispatcher manages passenger vehicles, routes, trips, intermediate stops and assignments. Routes and trips can be viewed, added and edited.
Cargo dispatcher manages trucks, cargo, shipments and shipment items. Cargo types are available for viewing.
Garage engineer manages the three vehicle types and mileage history, and calculates mileage for a date range.
Read-only user can browse tables and links and use the available reports and analytics. Write actions depend on the role. The active role appears at the bottom of the sidebar.
GuideRolesImage: The dropdown lists all five demo roles.
GuidePasswordTitle: Change your password or switch accounts
GuidePasswordText: Open Miscellaneous → Change password. Fill in Current password, New password and Repeat password. Save verifies the current password and saves the new one. Sign in again with the new password after the change succeeds. Back returns to Miscellaneous. To switch accounts, select Sign out at the bottom of the sidebar and sign in with a different username.
GuidePasswordImage: The password change screen. Save is below the three fields.
GuideSidebarText: Select the arrow next to Tables or Reference tables to expand or collapse the list. The Link tables group is at the bottom of Reference tables. Selecting a table opens its data in the workspace. Documents, Help and Miscellaneous first show their choices in the workspace. Analytics expands to show the dashboards available to your role. Scroll the sidebar to find lower entries. The bottom of the sidebar shows your username, role and the Sign out button.
GuideSidebarImage: The main window with Help selected. The available options appear on the right.
GuideReturningText: Back next to the heading opens the parent menu. For example, it returns from User guide to Help or from a report to Documents. Back to contents returns to the guide’s topic list. Back to the list appears after you follow a table link and restores the previous table with its search, sort order and page.
GuideKeyboardText: Tab moves focus to the next control and Shift+Tab to the previous one. Press Space to activate a focused button. Enter runs a table search when the search box has focus. Use the mouse wheel or scrollbar for long menus and forms. Drag the horizontal scrollbar at the bottom of a table to see columns farther right. Use the window’s title-bar buttons to minimize, maximize or close it.
GuideAboutText: Help → About lists the purpose of the course application, the course details and the technologies used. Back returns to the Help choices.
GuideSearchText: Open a table from the sidebar. Enter part of a displayed value such as a plate number, model or employee name. Select Search or press Enter. To clear the filter, empty the search box and select Search again. Click a column heading to sort by that column. Click it again to reverse the order. At the bottom, ‹ and › open the previous and next pages. The current page number is between them.
GuideSearchImage: The vehicle table. Search is above the rows, pagination below, and the record details are on the right.
GuideCardText: Add opens a new form on the right. To edit an existing record, select its row and change the fields in the details pane. Scroll the form to see the remaining fields. Save submits the values for validation and updates the table when the save succeeds. Cancel restores the selected row’s saved values or closes the new form. Save any changes you need before switching rows or sections. With read-only access, the details pane is for viewing.
GuideLookupText: Click the field or its arrow. Type part of a model, name or plate number directly into the field. The list shows matching records. Click a result or highlight it with ↑ and ↓ and press Enter. If there is one match, Enter selects it immediately. Esc closes the list and restores the last selected label. To clear an optional relation, clear the search text and select Unassigned. The form saves the selected record. If no records match, change the search or create the missing item in the reference table if your role permits it.
GuideLookupImage: The model selector combines the search box and dropdown in one field.
GuideDatePickerText: Type the date in the current language’s format, such as 23.11.2026 or 11/23/2026, or select the calendar icon and pick a day. The calendar arrows move between periods. Select the month heading to move up to month or year selection. Optional date fields can be cleared.
GuideOpenRelatedText: Select an underlined value in the table, such as a crew leader or model. To use the keyboard, select the linked cell and press Enter. If there are buttons under Related records in the details pane, select one to open a list filtered to the current record. Add in a filtered list preselects the parent record. Back to the list restores the previous screen.
GuideDeleteText: Select a row and choose Delete under its details. In the confirmation dialog, Delete removes the record and Cancel or Esc closes the dialog. Read the vehicle deletion message. Mileage readings and assignments may be removed with the vehicle. If another record prevents deletion, decide whether to reassign or remove the dependent entries within your permissions.
GuideDeleteImage: Vehicle deletion confirmation. Cancel keeps the record.
GuideVehiclePassportText: In Tables, select Passenger vehicle, Truck or Auxiliary vehicle. Each form has a vehicle passport with the plate, model, garage, status, mileage, color, engine number, body number, chassis number and inventory number. Enter the manufacture date. The last overhaul date is optional. Scroll down for type-specific fields. For a passenger vehicle, enter total capacity and a seat count within that capacity. Enter a truck’s load capacity in tonnes or an auxiliary vehicle’s usage intensity. Choose the model and garage from the reference tables. Before saving, check that manufacture and overhaul dates are on or before today, and that the overhaul is on or after manufacture. Plate, engine, body, chassis and inventory numbers must be unique. Mileage and usage intensity can be zero. Total capacity and load capacity must be positive.
GuideVehiclePassportImage: The lower part of the passenger vehicle form shows capacity and seat count.
GuideVehicleStatusText: Status is shown as text next to a colored marker. Operational means serviceable, Faulty means the vehicle needs repair, In repair means work is ongoing, and Retired means it is out of service. Open Analytics → Fleet condition and choose Vehicles requiring repair to see the current list of faulty vehicles.
GuideRepairsTitle: Record a repair and component work
GuideRepairsText:
A director opens Tables → Repair and selects Add. Enter the date, cost and work volume, find the vehicle by plate number, and choose a crew. Active marks work in progress. Saving an active repair changes an operational or faulty vehicle’s status to In repair. To complete the work, set Active to No and save. Closing the last active repair changes an In repair vehicle to Operational.
To record component repair or replacement, open Reference tables → Link tables → Component operation. Select the repair, component and operation type, then choose Save.
GuideRepairsImage: A repair with its linked vehicle, crew and Active field.
GuideMileageLogText: Open Tables → Mileage history. Select Add, find the vehicle by plate number, enter the date and cumulative odometer reading in kilometers, then select Save. Each vehicle can have one reading per date. To correct a reading, select its row, change the value and save. Enter mileage as a nonnegative whole number.
GuideMileageCalculationText: As a garage engineer, open Mileage history and expand Mileage calculation. Choose a vehicle and the start and end dates. Select Calculate. The result appears below the table. The application takes the latest reading on or before each date and calculates the difference. If either reading is missing, check the selected vehicle’s history.
GuideMileageCalculationImage: The engineer has selected a vehicle and dates. The calculated distance appears below the table.
GuideRoutesText: Open Tables → Route and select Add. Enter the route number and name, choose the start and end stops by name, and save. If a stop is missing, a director can add it in Reference tables → Stop. Passenger dispatchers can view, add and edit routes and trips. Directors can also delete them, subject to database constraints. Choose different start and end stops and use a unique route number.
GuideRoutesImage: A route with both endpoints. The table shows the linked stop names.
GuideIntermediatePointsText: Open Reference tables → Link tables → Intermediate stop. Select Add, choose the route and stop, and save. Repeat for other stops on the route. A stop can be added to a route once.
GuideRouteAssignmentTitle: Assign a bus to a route
GuideRouteAssignmentText: In Link tables, open Route assignment. Add a record, find the passenger vehicle by plate number, and choose the route by number or name. Save the assignment. When the bus changes routes, edit its existing assignment and choose the new route. A passenger vehicle can have one assignment.
GuideTripsText: Open Tables → Trip. Select Add, enter the date and passenger count, choose the bus by plate and the route by number or name, then save. To correct a trip, select its row and change the relevant fields. Saved trip passenger counts feed the Passengers by day metric in Analytics. Enter the passenger count as a nonnegative whole number.
GuideCargoCatalogText: Cargo types are stored in Reference tables → Cargo type. To register a cargo item, open Cargo and select Add. Enter its name, mass and volume, choose the type by name, and save. Directors can add cargo types. Cargo dispatchers choose from the existing list. Mass and volume must be positive.
GuideShipmentsText: Open Tables → Cargo shipment. Select Add, enter the date, and find the truck by plate number. Save the shipment. To make changes later, select the shipment row and edit its details.
GuideCargoItemsText: Select a saved shipment and choose Shipment cargo under Related records. Select Add, choose the cargo and enter the quantity. The shipment is already selected when you add from this filtered list. Save the item. If that cargo is already in the shipment, edit the quantity on its existing row. Back to the list returns to the shipment list. The full list of shipment items is also under Reference tables → Link tables. Enter the quantity as a positive whole number.
GuideCargoItemsImage: Items in the selected shipment. Back to the list returns to the shipment list.
GuideEmployeeText: Open Tables → Employee and select Add. Enter the last, first and middle names, gender, date of birth, years of experience and house number, then select the city and street. Save the record. Below the saved details are buttons for related employment records, crew membership, crews led by the employee and vehicle assignments. Scroll down in the details pane to see them.
GuideEmployeeImage: An employee record scrolled to the Related records buttons.
GuideEmploymentText: Open Employment record from Tables or from the employee details. Select Add. Enter the date and event type: hiring, termination or transfer. Enter a termination reason when applicable. Choose the document type and enter its date and number. Select the employee, job position, occupation, specialty, qualification, workplace and department. Save the record. The document date must be on or before the event date. A termination reason applies to a termination event.
GuideCrewsTitle: Create a crew and choose a leader
GuideCrewsText: In Tables → Crew, select Add. Enter the crew number and name, then find the leader by name or choose Unassigned. Save the record. Crews without a leader remain visible. Click an underlined name in the list to open the employee’s details. Use Crew membership to record a person’s membership separately.
GuideStaffAssignmentsTitle: Record crew membership and vehicle assignments
GuideStaffAssignmentsText: Under Reference tables → Link tables, open Crew membership. Choose an employee and a crew, then save. An employee can have one membership. To transfer them, edit the existing record. Vehicle assignment connects an employee to a vehicle selected by plate number. Each employee–vehicle pair can have one entry. Both lists can also be opened from the employee details.
GuideDirectoryUseText: Expand Reference tables in the sidebar and choose a table. Use the standard search and record details to find, add or edit entries. Create the records that other forms will need first. For example, create a Make, add a Model linked to that make, then add the vehicle. Write actions depend on the current role.
GuideDirectoryUseImage: The model catalogue. Each model is linked to a make in its details.
GuideDirectoryTransportText: Make stores manufacturer names. Model links a model name to its make. Garage stores the number and name of a vehicle’s garage. Component stores the names of parts and assemblies used in repair operations.
GuideDirectoryTrafficText: Stop stores the names of route endpoints and intermediate stops. Cargo type stores categories. Cargo stores names, mass, volume and the linked type. Select the cargo item from this catalogue when adding it to a shipment.
GuideDirectoryPersonnelText: City and Street supply an employee’s address. Job position stores the OKPDTR 2025 code and name. Occupation, Specialty and Qualification supply those fields in an employment record. Workplace and Department are used in the same form.
GuideReportTemplatesText: Open Documents and choose a template. Routes and endpoints shows the route number and name and the two endpoint names. Cargo shipments by date shows the date, plate number and truck model. Mileage readings shows the reading date, plate and cumulative mileage. The available templates depend on your role. Select Run to load the results into the table. Back returns to the template list. Directors and read-only users have all three templates. Passenger dispatchers have the route report, cargo dispatchers have the shipment report, and garage engineers have the mileage report. Manual SELECT is available to all five roles.
GuideReportTemplatesImage: The Routes and endpoints report with Run and CSV export controls.
GuideManualSelectText:
In Documents, select Manual SELECT. The SQL query box already contains an example. Replace it with your query or choose Run to try the example.
SELECT id, name FROM public.model ORDER BY id LIMIT 20
One read-only SELECT is supported over the report sources available to your role. You can use DISTINCT, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY and LIMIT, aliases with AS, and COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, LOWER and UPPER. The server returns up to 500 rows, accepts up to 32 columns and limits SQL execution to four seconds. Select the columns you need and add a WHERE condition to narrow the results. Sources include routes, stops, trips, cargo shipments, mileage history, makes, models, garages and vehicle tables. Use the table name from the schema, for example public.model.
GuideManualSelectImage: The Manual SELECT editor showing a query over models and its results.
GuideCsvText: After running a report, select Export CSV. In the save dialog, choose a folder, enter a filename and select Save. Cancel closes the dialog. The CSV contains the current result, using localized headings where available. Run the report again to refresh the data. For import into Excel, use UTF-8 and the delimiter that matches the export language.
GuideAnalyticsPeriodText: Expand Analytics in the main sidebar and select a dashboard under its group heading. Set Date from, Date to and other filters, then choose Apply. Both dates are included in a range of 1 to 366 days. Reset restores the screen defaults. An invalid range leaves the last valid result on screen. While Analytics is open, data refreshes every five seconds using the applied filters. Applied filters are kept as you switch screens during the current session.
GuideAnalyticsPeriodImage: Company overview. The dashboard links are under the expanded Analytics item in the main sidebar.
GuideAnalyticsMetricsTitle: Read dashboards and drill into results
GuideAnalyticsMetricsText: Overview cards open the corresponding dashboard with the same date range. Fleet condition shows the current snapshot. The Vehicles requiring repair card filters for faulty vehicles. Click a bar in a route, truck, crew or vehicle ranking to apply that filter. In Truck utilization, group the heat map by date or weekday. Scroll it horizontally for longer periods. In Vehicle mileage, garage and category narrow the vehicle picker, and the result shows the dates of both readings. Available dashboards depend on your role.
GuideAnalyticsExportTitle: Save the chart as PNG or PDF
GuideAnalyticsExportText: Select Export below the chart you need. Choose PNG or PDF in the file type list, then choose a folder and filename. Both formats include the chart title, applied date range or snapshot date, and chart units. To save a different range, apply the new dates and export again.
GuideInterfaceText: Open Miscellaneous → Settings. Under Interface, choose a light or dark theme. Text size offers Normal, Large and Extra large. Language offers Русский and English. Each change is applied and saved immediately. Settings are loaded at the next launch and apply to all application accounts under the current Windows profile.
GuideInterfaceImage: Settings in the dark theme, including Interface, Accessibility, Tables and the reset button.
GuideAccessibilityText: Select Color vision accessibility mode under Accessibility. It changes the accent colors in both light and dark themes. Vehicle statuses also have text labels, and charts retain their labels and values. Clear the checkbox to turn the mode off.
GuideDensityText: Under Tables, choose Normal for standard row height or Compact to fit more rows on screen. Text size is a separate setting. Tables can be scrolled vertically and horizontally.
GuideResetText: Reset settings immediately restores the light theme, normal text size, Russian language and normal row density. It also turns off color vision accessibility mode. These values are saved in the local Windows profile. If a save error appears, check access to %LOCALAPPDATA%\BD_RGR.
GuideConnectionProblemsText: If the local API is unavailable, check that it is running and that clientsettings.json points to the same address and port. Use Start-Autopark.ps1 from the project folder to start the API and client together. If the message names a Database setting in the server’s appsettings.Local.json, pass that setting name to the person managing the server. For a database request error, check whether PostgreSQL is running and whether the database name, connection settings and service account permissions match the project README.
GuideConnectionProblemsImage: The local API error appears below the sign-in buttons.
GuideAccountProblemsText: If credentials are rejected, check the keyboard layout and Caps Lock and try again. If the username is taken, choose another one. If the passwords differ, re-enter both. If the demo role list is empty, select Back to sign-in and reopen Registration. If the session has ended, sign in again. If a message opens in a separate dialog, select OK to close it.
GuideDataProblemsTitle: Empty tables, permissions and write errors
GuideDataProblemsText: No matching records means the current selection contains no rows available to you. Clear the search and choose Search. If an action is hidden or denied, check your role at the bottom of the sidebar. For a field error, read its label and message, fill the required value or correct the format. If a linked record is unavailable, reopen the selector and choose it again. If a unique value is already in use, edit the existing row or use a different value.
GuideReportProblemsText: For a SELECT error, check table and column names, source availability for your role and the supported SQL syntax. If a query times out, narrow it with a filter. If the chart is empty, check the metric and date order. If saving a CSV, PNG, or PDF fails, choose a folder where you can write files.
